title: Prove the mechanism before the model
subtitle: Three load-bearing ideas behind the custom decoder, a device-side graph loop, a persisting L2 window and a constant-memory trie mask, were each proved on the real GPU in a small lab before the model existed, and one of them contradicted the documentation

lede: The custom decoder for the tool-discovery model, told in Constraint made cheaper than no constraint, rests on three mechanisms that the whole design assumes will work: a decode loop that runs on the device under a graph whose continuation predicate the GPU itself writes, a window of L2 cache set aside so the model's weights stay resident between tokens, and a trie-shaped grammar mask served from constant memory. If any of the three had not worked on the generation of GPU I had, the decoder would have been built on sand. So before the model was trained, each was built and measured on its own, on the real card, with a toy body.
quote: The decoder was then built on three numbers rather than three hopes.
evidence: Hardware-first prototyping: three decoder mechanisms each proved on the real GPU in a small lab with a toy body before the model was trained.
CUDA graphs and device-side control flow: a decode loop under a graph with a conditional node, 4.304 µs saved per token per kernel.
GPU cache tuning: an L2 persisting window whose set-aside ceiling measured 60 MiB of the 96 MiB L2, against what the documentation suggests.
Constant-memory kernel design: a grammar mask consulted in 0.016 µs at a 131,072-token vocabulary.
author: Corey James
